title: COMING JULY 18th & 19th | All Jammed Up Music Festival
location: One World Brewing – West, 520 Haywood Rd, Asheville, North Carolina, 28806
description:
July 18th &19th, 2026 | One World Brewing West | Tickets from $30.00 click here! 
The All Jammed Up Fest is back BIGGER and BETTER this year with Kendall Street Company headlining Saturday and Sicard Hollow headlining Sunday. Plus, touring bands like Frute and Keep, as well as staples of the Asheville music scene – Suns of Stars, Strictly Liquid, and more!

Presented by All Jammed Up, this special two-night party celebrates community and the joy of live music. Come kick your shoes off, dance your heart out, and support local artists and vendors! You’re not gonna want to miss it!



Virginia’s Kendall Street Company are no strangers to having a wild time. The genre-fluid, eclectic rock ensemble has drawn varied comparisons to the dynamic jams of Umphrey’s McGee and Widespread Panic, songwriting prowess of John Prine, experimental psychedelia of Pink Floyd, progressive jazz-infused rock of Frank Zappa, and off-color humor of Ween and They Might Be Giants. Including elements of crowd participation, off-the-cuff comedic bits, haphazard choreography, musical improvisation, and surprise musical guests, each Kendall Street Company concert is an experience unlike any other. You’ll laugh, you’ll cry. Just remember to stay hydrated.

Nashville’s psychedelic punk-grass rockers, Sicard Hollow, is a four-piece progressive bluegrass band who formed with a mutual passion for pushing the boundaries of genre. Heavily influenced by the Grateful Dead and New Grass Revival, these young pickers bring new energy to a timeless style with a combination of fearless improvisation and instrumental prowess.

Frute is a psych rock collective out of Atlanta featuring Alo Ver’s ethereal vocals, which complement the band’s deep pocket grooves and iridescent soundscapes.


Orbiting around Asheville’s grateful music scene since late 2023, Suns Of Stars blends contemporary and traditional bluegrass with a high energy jam style.
At its core lies the trio of Alex Bazemore (guitar), and Asheville’s own Jackson Chisholm (upright bass) and Johnny Humphries (mandolin), son of local Bluegrass legend Don Humphries. As Suns Of Stars has been gathering momentum they’ve picked up Alex Ball (fiddle) and Jason Flournoy (banjo). Suns Of Stars members are all hometown heros in various musical projects around town which has led to great turnout at their shows. That, along with a massive song repertoire and growing list of original music make for a unique performance each time.


Fireside Collective has become a true hybrid, with a strong foundation in bluegrass and folk, and healthy doses of rock n’ roll and funk, all blended together in a unique and colorful amalgam of original music.

Strictly Liquid is a musical collaboration of creative spirits blending funky, psychedelic jams and rock and roll through improv!

Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

title: Art Church - Make Art from a Slow Quiet Place - ONLINE
description:
Awakening Asheville
Hosted by Tish Sjoberg

2nd and 4th Sundays

Now On-Line during Covid-19 Quarantine
10:00 a.m. – 12:15 p.m.
$0 - $25 (Included in our monthly pass)

Slow down and be with yourself through art making. A rich morning that feeds your spirit, rests your body, quiets your mind and helps you remember who you are!

Here we will use the arts to have a conversation with ourselves and connect to our longings and gifts. This is not about religion, yet in the inquiry you may choose to make connections to your religious beliefs.

The format: We check in as a group, we may do a little drumming, have 5 minutes of quiet/reflection/meditation/prayer/relaxation time, go create art in silence (without talking) doing our own thing and then come back together to honor what we spent our time doing.

Art making can be painting, writing, sand tray, collage, doodling, scribbling, sewing, mixed media, movement, or…. No previous art experience necessary just the willingness to follow what you are attracted to and moving slow and quiet.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Mary Cassatt: Painting the Modern Woman
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Mary Cassatt: Painting the Modern Woman follows the progression of Cassatt’s work, her meticulous study of the Old Masters and traditional techniques while also exposing her frustration at not finding a style that truly expressed her desire to be modern until she discovered the Impressionists. This film tells a riveting tale of great social and cultural change at a time when women were fighting for their rights and the language of art was being completely re-written. Mary Cassatt and her modern women were at the heart of it all.

title: Explore the Museum of Costume Jewelry
description:
Asheville Introverts

According to their website, "The Museum of Costume Jewelry is dedicated to the collection, preservation, research, and exhibition of 20th century costume jewelry." We'll wander the museum together, and for those who are interested we may walk to a cafe afterward to discuss some of our favorite pieces. For more information about the museum, please visit their website: [https://museumofcostumejewelry.com/](https://museumofcostumejewelry.com/)

While no admission fee is listed on their website, the museum is a 501(c)3 nonprofit organization and accepts donations. They also have a gift shop, so bring your wallet if you are a fan of shiny things!

**Parking**
Street parking is extremely limited by the museum, so I would recommend parking in garage instead. The Rankin Avenue garage is just around the block from the museum located at 68 Rankin Avenue.

title: Summer Art Camp | Appalachian Arts & Crafts (Rising 9th - 12th grade)
location: NC
description:
REGISTER HERE 
Blending creativity with cultural heritage, students will explore the artistic traditions of Appalachian culture through a series of hands-on crafts. They will begin the week creating vibrant painted barn quilts and learning basic weaving techniques with natural materials. They’ll spend the remainder of the week further developing their weaving skills to make reed baskets and needle felting a landscape.   
Meet the Instructor: Kati Robbins
Kati Robbins has over 12 years of experience as an art educator, teaching studio arts and crafts to a wide range of age groups in different learning environments. She is currently based in Asheville where she works as a high school art teacher. Her creative work focuses on mixed media and assemblage, with a strong interest in collaborative and community based projects. She is inspired by Appalachian craft traditions, natural materials and the surrounding landscape. When Kati isn’t teaching or making art, she enjoys gardening, cooking, reading and hiking in the mountains.

title: Summer Art Camp | Exploring Photography Without a Camera (Rising 9th – 12th grade)
location: NC
description:
REGISTER HERE 
Photography doesn’t always require a camera. In this experimental image lab, students will explore photography-based processes that use light, chemistry, and transfer techniques to create images. Through hands-on exploration of cyanotypes, lumen prints, pinhole photography, and image transfers, students will experiment with transparency, layering, and transformation—creating works that blur the line between photography, printmaking, and mixed media.     
Meet the Instructor: Kristina Shriver
Kristina Shriver is a visual art educator with over 16 years of experience, working with students of all ages. She teaches at Asheville High School and serves as an AP Studio Art Reader and mentor for other art educators. Kristina designs hands-on, material-rich art experiences that connect historical techniques to contemporary practice, emphasizing experimentation, personal storytelling, and meaningful creative exploration.

title: Art Loeb at BRP to Pilot Mtn - 6.3 Mi, 1900 Ft EG
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**Details**

* 6 Miles, 2000 Ft elevation gain
* Carpool meeting time is 8:00 at the Asheville Tanger Outlets parking lot behind the Waffle House.
* Sign up starts Friday at 8pm

I am going to try this hike again although the weather currently doesn't look promising for up in that area on Monday. This is a nice out and back along the Art Loeb trail to Pilot Mountain which has a beautiful view at the turn around. Some of the trail is a bit overgrown although not bad and I recommend long pants. We will keep a moderate pace dependent on the terrain but with limited stops. **Although the distance and elevation might sound like a moderate hike, most of the elevation gain comes in the last 1.5 miles. It felt like a much harder hike when I scouted because of that so please don't sign up unless you are okay for a challenge at the end with no way to go but up**.

I enjoy stopping at the Pisgah Inn after the hike and sitting in the rocking chairs behind the hotel. They have a convenience store where you can buy drinks and sandwiches or you can bring your own. We will try to break up into cars that want to do that and want to just go back to the carpool area.

https://www.alltrails.com/explore/custom-routes/uploaded-route-72e4032

**CARPOOL**
We will meet at the Asheville Outlets behind the Waffle House at 8:00. It is about a 50 minute ride to the trailhead. Please be there a little early so we can leave at 8:00 for the trailhead. There is very limited parking at the trailhead and it is all along the side of the road. If you plan to meet us at the trailhead, plan to be there by 8:50. See the AllTrails link above for directions to the trailhead.

**WEATHER**
I'll watch the weather and post a cancellation message by 7:00 AM if the forecast is >50% chance of precipitation.

**QUESTIONS?**
You can message me through MeetUp until 9:00 AM the day of. Cell reception may be sketchy, but you can try to text or call me up to the start of the hike: (508) 965-2333.

**LEGALESE**

title: Craven Gap
description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0
This is a fairly undulating hike. It's narrow at first with some rocky steps and then narrow and rooty for most of the way until halfway when there's a short climb to the 2.5 mile mark. We go about 2.7 to 2.9 mph.

Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome to attend.

When you arrive, park at the gravel lot on the other side of the road, closest to Town Mountain. You'll see some people gathering by their cars.

Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people.
When you arrive, we'll circle up and introduce ourselves briefly. There will be a person who is a sweep. This person is the person who walks last and makes sure no one gets lost.

We leave the parking spot at 9:10. If someone needs a nature break, we wait fo you, but it's not a hike where we stop and take photos or frequent breaks. We basically keep hiking until the 1/2 way mark, then turn around after a short (approximately 5 minute) break. Then we keep that same pace on the way back. If we get on a trail right at 9:10, we are normally finished around 10:50.

These are out and back hikes, meaning that we hike in and turn around half way to return back.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

title: Warp, Weft, and the Grid: Member Preview
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
As a valued Museum Member, we invite you to join us for the exclusive preview of our newest exhibition—Warp, Weft, and the Grid. 
4–5pm | Upper-Level Members 
Register Here 
5–7pm | All Members 
Register Here 
6–7pm  |  Curator Talk 
Limited capacity—program preregistration required 
 
Co-curator of Warp, Weft, and the Grid, Kathleen Curtis Wilson will present a series of photographs and share personal stories about her collection of bed coverlets woven by women in southern Appalachia, 1850–1930. Please note this program has limited capacity—program preregistration is required. Learn more. 
About the Exhibition
Warp, Weft, and the Grid highlights the artistic significance of 19th and early 20th-century southern Appalachian coverlets, exploring how the designs of these handwoven textiles anticipated many of the same visually arresting motifs at the heart of Modernist geometric abstraction in later 20th century art. The exhibition displays historic coverlets alongside works ranging from the color theory experiments and avant-garde weavings of Josef and Anni Albers to Julian Stanczak’s dynamic optical illusions, and even early computer-based art, emphasizing their shared visual language. It offers new perspectives on women’s artistic labor as well as the material history and experimental ethos of weavers in the region, foregrounding the remarkable artistic and technical merit of the artists who made them. 
Sponsored in part by Fleur Bresler. 
Please note:
Exhibition Previews are reserved for current Museum Members; please only register Members included in your membership.

title: Curator's Talk | Hidden in Plain View—Art in Southern Appalachia
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
*Limited capacity—preregistration is required* 
Co-curator of Warp, Weft, and the Grid, Kathleen Curtis Wilson 
Curator Kathleen Curtis Wilson will present a series of photographs and share personal stories about her collection of bed coverlets woven by women in southern Appalachia, 1850–1930. An appreciation of Appalachian weaving was hindered by stereotypical images of Appalachia as a poverty-ridden, art-poor region. These images and a lack of women’s material culture studies in the region once made it easy to dismiss Appalachia as void of objects of art, creativity, and design worthy of national attention. 
Today, graphic artists and laypersons will appreciate the simple designs of early coverlet patterns for the straight lines, accuracy, and bold color choices of this distinctive artistic tradition. 
The woven coverlets images presented during Wilson’s presentation make it apparent that many southern Appalachian weavers did not put away their looms in the nineteenth century but made a conscious decision to continue to weave and preserve beautiful objects for their own pleasure, as gifts for family members, or in celebration of important events. 
Kathleen Curtis Wilson is the author of five non-fiction books: The Quiet Work of Women (2001, reprinting 2026); Uplifting the South—Mary Mildred Sullivan’s Legacy for Appalachia (2005); Irish People, Irish Linen (2011); Dancing at the Warm Springs Hotel (2022); and Adventurous Max Flax (2023), an educational children’s book. Her first novel, The Fabric of Wishful Thinking. (available 2026). 
Wilson served as honorary fellow at both University of Ulster, Northern Ireland, and Virginia Humanities, Charlottesville, Virginia. She has given scores of public speeches and lectures at professional conferences in the United States and abroad. Born in Michigan, Wilson studied weaving at The Cranbrook Schools. She established and operated Old Abingdon Weavers in Southwest Virginia from 1983–1993. She lives in Blacksburg, Virginia.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Bent Creek/Arboretum -- 6 mi, 900 ft. elev. gain
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**Sign-ups open Sunday, July 12, 8:00 PM**

This is a walk in the forest along varied trails, including some one-lane gravel roads that are good for side-by-side socializing. It's mostly easy-going on gradual hills, with a couple of moderately strenuous areas. Several trail segments are cobbled together to give us around six miles in all. Not too hard, but not for beginners if you've never done this sort of thing. I give it a 3.5 difficulty level. We'll take a **15-minute** rest around halfway through for a water break and snack if you'd like to bring something.

Well-behaved dogs are welcome, but the Forestry Service requires leashes for all. Sturdy hiking shoes/boots are recommended. Most people won't need poles for this one.

**MEETING TIME & PLACE**
We'll meet at Bent Creek River Park. Please come early for sign-in & introductions so we can leave promptly at 9:00 AM.

Here's the location on Google Maps: [https://goo.gl/maps/Wtw2zi8K4eKFuDHUA](https://goo.gl/maps/Wtw2zi8K4eKFuDHUA)

**GUESTS**
If you'd like to bring a guest, they should join the Asheville Hiking Group and sign up for the hike on their own. Alternatively, contact me in advance and ask if it's okay to bring a "+1" after you've made it onto the "Going" list. Depending on timing and demand, I may be able to add your guest.

**COURTESY TO WAITLISTERS (Please!!)**
Only sign up if you \*truly\* plan to come. If you must cancel, please change your status to "Not Going" as soon as possible. Avoid dropping out within 18 hours of the hike so wait-listers can have sufficient notice. And please please PLEASE don't be a no-show.

We'll watch the weather and post a cancellation message by 7:30 AM on the morning of the hike if the forecast is >50% chance of precipitation.

**LEGALESE**
This Asheville Hiking Group event involves hiking and, possibly, transportation to and from the meetup site. Participants are responsible for their own safety and affirm that they have the appropriate skills, physical conditioning, equipment, and supplies. Hiking may involve risks to oneself and property. Neither your hike organizer nor Asheville Hiking Group can assure your safety nor eliminate all risks. Participants assume full responsibility for any injuries, damages, or losses.

title: Craven Gap
description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0
This is a fairly undulating hike. It's narrow at first with some rocky steps and then narrow and rooty for most of the way until halfway when there's a short climb to the 2.5 mile mark. We go about 2.7 to 2.9 mph.

Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome to attend.

When you arrive, park at the gravel lot on the other side of the road, closest to Town Mountain. You'll see some people gathering by their cars.

Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people.
When you arrive, we'll circle up and introduce ourselves briefly. There will be a person who is a sweep. This person is the person who walks last and makes sure no one gets lost.

We leave the parking spot at 9:10. If someone needs a nature break, we wait fo you, but it's not a hike where we stop and take photos or frequent breaks. We basically keep hiking until the 1/2 way mark, then turn around after a short (approximately 5 minute) break. Then we keep that same pace on the way back. If we get on a trail right at 9:10, we are normally finished around 10:50.

These are out and back hikes, meaning that we hike in and turn around half way to return back.

description:
Join Kathleen Wilson, co-curator of Warp, Weft, and the Grid, for an introduction to her debut novel, The Fabric of Wishful Thinking. 
This richly researched portrait of 1910 rural Appalachia is written by an author with deep expertise in Appalachian history, craft, and culture. Along with its compelling story, Wilson’s book offers a rare look inside early Southern textile mill culture. The Fabric of Wishful Thinking is a powerful story about families and the fractures that result from divided loyalties. Ella Hutchinson’s story offers a portrait of female resilience during a time without legal protections for mothers and wives. It is a gripping novel about friendship, motherhood, first love, and irrevocable loss.

title: Biltmore Estate: Walk the Westover Green and Blue Trails
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Located at The Inn on Biltmore Estate, the Westover Green and Blue Trails provide access to some of Biltmore's beautiful woodlands. We will loop the Green Trail in a clockwise direction, pick up the Blue Trail to walk its entire length, and then go back to get the rest of the Green Trail.

I estimate this to be about 4.5 miles. The Green Trail is wide. The Blue Trail is of moderate width. These are relatively easy trails. There is a little elevation change, but nothing particularly strenuous.

When you drive to the Inn, you will turn onto its access road. Near the entrance to the Inn is the entrance to the parking area. There are two rows of parking, an upper row closer to the Inn, and a lower row a little further from the Inn. We will gather on the lower row at the far end (away from the Inn).

If you need a restroom prior to the walk, Antler Hill is very close and there are public restrooms there. No restroom facilities are available during the walk.

Dress appropriately for the weather. Tennis shoes are fine, unless it has rained a lot recently, in which case you will probably want light hiking boots. Most won't want walking sticks, though I plan to take just one. As always, bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dogs on leash are welcome. Strollers designed for trail use would be ok.

There is a grounds admission fee. We walk at Biltmore several times each year, so an annual grounds pass is highly recommended.

Many regular Biltmore guests have never walked the Westover Trails. I think you will enjoy these.

title: Collective Liberation: A BIPOC-Led Community Event
description:
Psychedelic Society of Asheville
Please join us on Saturday, July 18, 2026, from 11:00 AM –1:00 PM at [Third Room](https://thirdroom.art/) in Asheville for **Collective Liberation: Subverting Segregation Through The Psychedelic Healing Arts**.

This will be a meaningful gathering rooted in connection, healing, and collective possibility.
We're honored to welcome [COHOBA](https://cohoba.org/), North Carolina's first psychedelic-positive, BIPOC-led nonprofit organization based out of Charolette.

COHOBA’s work is transforming the landscape of wellness through mental health services, somatic care, creative expression, and community-centered healing. Grounded in the understanding that true wellness emerges through relationship, culture, and collective care, COHOBA is helping reimagine what accessible and inclusive healing can look like.

This special event is an opportunity to meet COHOBA co-founders [Laura Camilo](https://cohoba.org/our-team/), MSW, LCSW, and [Daniel De La Cruz](https://cohoba.org/our-team/), MSW, LCSW, hear the inspiring story behind their work, and engage in meaningful conversation with others who share a vision for a more connected world.

Together, we'll explore how communities can become powerful spaces for healing, belonging, and transformation. We'll reflect on expanding access to care, fostering resilience, and creating more inclusive pathways for wellness and psychedelic education and exploration.

Whether you're deeply involved in this work or simply curious to learn more, you'll find a welcoming space where lived experience is honored, questions are encouraged, and genuine connection can flourish.

This is a donation-based event, with a suggested contribution of **$15–$30**. No one will be turned away due to lack of funds. Please complete your registration and submit your donation via Venmo ([@psysocietyavl](https://account.venmo.com/u/psysocietyavl)), and include “COHOBA” in the payment note. Your donation directly supports community-centered programming, accessible healing spaces, and the continued growth of COHOBA's mission and vision.

Come be part of an afternoon of inspiration, connection, and collective imagination. We look forward to gathering with you all in Asheville.

title: Copperhead Trail at Haywood Community College on National Ice Cream Day
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
It's likely to be hot, so at the end of the walk we will go get an ice cream together.

To get to the Copperhead Trail from our start point, we will go clockwise on the Bobcat Trail, and then take the Kingfisher Trail to the Copperhead Trail. When we intersect with the Millpond Connector, we will turn left, finishing the campus loop on the Bobcat Trail. All together, it isn't over 2 miles. Part of the walk is on pavement, part on well-groomed trail, and part on not-as-well groomed trail. There is some small elevation change.

As you enter the campus from Jones Cove Road, go to the first parking lot on the left. We will gather there and then head out.

Be sure to dress for the weather. I'm going to wear tennis shoes, unless it has rained a lot recently (in which case, I will wear light hiking boots). I plan to bring one walking stick, just in case. As always, you are urged to bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Trail strollers should not have any problem. There are no bathrooms available on a Sunday afternoon, so take care of such needs before you arrive.

title: Burton St Community Association Monthly Meeting
Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: In Conversation | Learning to See: Photographer Hazel Larsen Archer at Black Mountain College
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join summer intern Sophie Weiser as she explores the incredible life and work of Hazel Larsen Archer, the first full-time photography teacher at Black Mountain College (BMC). During her nine years at BMC (1944-1953) Archer developed her unique method of “learning to see” using the camera as a tool. Weiser’s talk will also explore Archer’s experience with disability and how she navigated life on BMC Campus while producing a dazzling array of photos, including her captivating portraits of fellow BMC students and teachers, such as Josef and Anni Albers, Ruth Asawa, and Merce Cunningham.    
Bio: 
Sophie Weiser is a summer intern at the Asheville Art Museum, working with the Learning and Engagement Department’s Summer Art Camp. She is going into her third year at Trinity College Dublin, where she majors in Classics, Ancient History and Archaeology, with a focus in Classical Civilization. From the ages of three to seven she lived with her parents and twin sister in Asheville, and has continued to return to the area throughout her life. Her time in the robust local art scene of Asheville and its surrounding areas has been integral in developing her commitment to and involvement with the arts and museum world.

title: Modern Pop Art Experience with Michael Albert
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join us as Michael Albert leads a Hands-On Collage workshop where participants will have the chance to create their own masterpieces using cereal boxes and other colorful cardboard packaging. All participants will receive a free signed poster of one of Albert’s creations as a special gift for joining him in this creative art making experience.  
His nationally renowned “Modern Pop Art Experience” Art programs will have toured more than 100 cities in six states this summer including: Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, Georgia, South Carolina & North Carolina.  Over the past 15 years he has been running this art enrichment program and brought it to more than 1,500 libraries, museums, schools, art and community centers in 48 states so far. 
American Pop Artist Michael Albert was born and raised in New York on Long Island where he graduated from New York University with a business degree. Albert is the author of an artist autobiography titled, “An Artist’s America” (Henry Holt, 2008). His work has been described as a cross between Pop Art, Cubism and Recycling.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Mary Cassatt: Painting the Modern Woman
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Mary Cassatt: Painting the Modern Woman follows the progression of Cassatt’s work, her meticulous study of the Old Masters and traditional techniques while also exposing her frustration at not finding a style that truly expressed her desire to be modern until she discovered the Impressionists. This film tells a riveting tale of great social and cultural change at a time when women were fighting for their rights and the language of art was being completely re-written. Mary Cassatt and her modern women were at the heart of it all.

location: NC
description:
JOIN THE WAITLIST 
Students will explore art and the environment through a series of mixed-media projects. Students will create collages of animal habitats using recycled materials and mountain landscapes featuring local wildlife. Students will be encouraged to use personal expression, gain environmental awareness, and learn creative problem-solving. Students will conclude the week by creating mixed-media memory boxes or shadow boxes filled with hand-built clay creatures.  
Meet the Instructor: Julia Worden
Julia Worden holds a master’s degree in art education and teaches visual art in Western North Carolina. She is passionate about working with learners of all ages and is dedicated to fostering confidence, critical thinking, and the development of individual artistic voices. Having spent seven years living abroad, Julia engaged extensively with galleries, artistic events, and diverse art communities across Europe, experiences she now weaves into her teaching to deepen students’ understanding and connection to art. Outside the studio and classroom, she enjoys reading, baking, and spending time with her cats, Cas and Nyx.

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Walk at Little Champion Plant in Waynesville on National Ice Cream Sandwich Day
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Old Timers call this property on Old Howell Mill Road near Old Asheville Highway "Little Champion" because the Canton Champion Paper Mill put in this plant to put wax on paper for making milk cartons. The Mill changed hands several times, but the Old Timers kept calling it Little Champion. (Note that Google Maps calls it Evergreen Packaging, and the sign on the building now says Suzano.)

The 3/4-mile walking track at Little Champion runs by Richland Creek with lots of creekside trees, by fishing spots, and by a picnic area. There is a bathroom in the middle of the track. We plan to do 4 counterclockwise laps. (Yes, you are free to do fewer or even more!) That will make a total of 5 KM/3.1 miles.

Be sure you enter the property on the Old Asheville Highway (east) side of the plant (the side with the Suzano sign) on Ken Thompson Drive, go to the rear of the building, and then turning left, go ***all the way to the far end of the back of the parking lot, down by the sign designating the Drop Lot***. It is in that corner of the parking lot where we will assemble. (If you go down the stairs into the middle of the track, you will be in the wrong place and will miss where the group is assembling.)

Dress appropriately for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. There is a little hill on each lap, so some may want walking sticks. Bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack. This is a paved track, so tennis shoes will be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers will have no problem.

Since it is National Ice Cream Sandwich Day, at the end of the walk we will have available free ice cream sandwiches for our walkers. Now, how's that for a hot summer afternoon!

title: Fantasy and Sci-Fi Silent Book Club
description:
Asheville Introverts
BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles at Day Trip! We will likely be in the large ‘back room’ (with the Disco Ball and under the large white cat)

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather, grab drinks and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. We want to know what you're reading! Organic dialogue welcome!

location: NC
description:
REGISTER HERE 
Students will explore art and the environment through a series of mixed-media projects. Students will create collages of animal habitats using recycled materials and mountain landscapes featuring local wildlife. Students will be encouraged to use personal expression, gain environmental awareness, and learn creative problem-solving. Students will conclude the week by creating mixed-media memory boxes or shadow boxes filled with hand-built clay creatures.  
Meet the Instructor: Julia Worden
Julia Worden holds a master’s degree in art education and teaches visual art in Western North Carolina. She is passionate about working with learners of all ages and is dedicated to fostering confidence, critical thinking, and the development of individual artistic voices. Having spent seven years living abroad, Julia engaged extensively with galleries, artistic events, and diverse art communities across Europe, experiences she now weaves into her teaching to deepen students’ understanding and connection to art. Outside the studio and classroom, she enjoys reading, baking, and spending time with her cats, Cas and Nyx.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Movies on the Green: School of Rock
description:
Bring a blanket or lawn chair and head to Reynolds Green for UNC Asheville’s Movies on the Green summer film series! Before the movie begins, enjoy lawn games,  and music starting at 7:30 p.m. Hilltop Ice Cream will also be on site with treats available for purchase. 
The movie will begin at dusk, approximately 8:30 p.m. Outside food is welcome, but alcohol is not permitted. Designated accessible seating areas will be available, and captioning will be enabled when available for each film.  
The event is free and open to the public, with free parking available after 5 p.m. on screening day. Parking in nearby lots P27, P13, and P28 is recommended. Click here to view the campus map.  
This event is part of the Movies on the Green summer film series, which included screenings of A League of Their Own on June 26 and Jumanji on July 17. All screenings take place on the Reynolds Green and are free and open to the public.

UNC Asheville is committed to providing universal access to all of our events. title: 5 KM/3 mile Sunday Afternoon Walk in Canton
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
The start/finish point is the parking lot for the Rec Park baseball field (not to be confused with the public-school baseball field next to the football stadium—our meeting place is a little further down the road). The field has been rebuilt since Hurricane Helene, and the parking area is still there. Hopefully, some of the Clyde Elementary School Cardinals Elite Walking Team and their families will be joining us for this event.

We will start our walk at the Canton Recreation Park, go past Pisgah High School, up to the public library and the historic cemetery, down Academy Street, and through part of downtown on our way back to Canton Greenway and the start point. The up and down are fairly steep.

Dress appropriately for the weather. Consider a hat and sunscreen. Tennis shoes are fine. This is all pavement, but some might want walking sticks for the up and down; I plan to walk with a pair of walking sticks. Bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack. Dogs on leash are welcome. Some of the sidewalk along well-traveled roads is narrow and some is not in the best condition, so strollers and wheelchairs are not recommended.

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers!

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.***

* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary.

See you at the table!

title: Thursday Run
description:
Asheville Runners
Come run 1, 3, or 6 miles and stay for a beer and soccer tennis after at Olde London Road.

Routes-
1 miler:
RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.
RIGHT on River Arts Place
Cross Riverside onto the Greenway
Right on the Greenway to the Craven St Park put in (the dock)
Turn around and go back the same way to OLR

3 miler:
Start the same as 1 miler
Continue onto Craven St. Bridge
LEFT onto Greenway after bridge
Follow Greenway all the way until it ends at Haywood Rd.
RIGHT onto Haywood Rd, go across the bridge
Cross the Roundabout at Roberts St. and continue onto Clingman
Continue on Clingman
LEFT onto Owens Bell Lane
LEFT onto Hilliard at the top of the hill
LEFT onto W Haywood, follow all the way down to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts
Follow Roberts back to OLR
Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

6 miler:
After the W Haywood downhill to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts St. take to Lyman and head back to the Greenway
LEFT onto the Greenway, take all the way to Amboy
RIGHT on Amboy to cross the bridge
RIGHT into French Broad River Park, run the loop at the park
Cross back over the bridge on Amboy and run the Greenway back to the roundabout
Follow Lyman back to OLR

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Walk the Ethnobotany Trail and More at the NC Arboretum
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Meet inside the Baker Visitor Center which opens at 9:00 a.m. Restrooms are available at the start point. We will start walking as soon as everyone has arrived, hopefully no later than 9:05.

The walk is a guided 5 KM trail. There are some moderate hills and stair climbing. A significant part of the route is on well-groomed trails with very few obstacles. Some people will want walking poles.

We will walk down Running Cedar Road to Bent Creak Road. Going down Bent Creek Road, we will turn onto the Ethnobotany Trail, and then back onto Bent Creek Road. We will go back up Wesley Branch Trail to the Willow Pond and thence back to the start point.

Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. Sneakers should be fine, unless it has rained recently. Be sure to bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack.

Dogs on leash are welcome but are not allowed in buildings or in the Bonsai Exhibit. Trail strollers should be ok.

The NC Arboretum does not have an admission fee, but they charge $25 per car parking fee (so pack as many people in your car as you can). We recommend the driver purchase the lowest level annual membership which includes free parking. (Of course, you may want a higher-level membership, your choice.) We walk at the Arboretum at least six times per year.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Body Process Class: Circuitry
description:
Access Consciousness® Asheville
## What If Your Body Has Been Waiting for This?

## **You’re Invited: Access Consciousness Body Process Class**

What if your body isn’t something to fix…
but something to listen to?

What if it has been whispering (or maybe shouting) for your attention in ways you were never taught to understand?

I’d love to invite you to a beautiful, hands-on **Access Consciousness Body Process class** — a space where you get to receive, gift, and explore a different communion with bodies.

### What Is a Body Process?

Access Consciousness Body Processes are gentle, hands-on techniques that invite the body to:
• Release stored trauma and shock
• Activate natural capacities
• Undo limitations held in tissue and cellular memory
• Restore communication between you and your body

This isn’t massage.
It isn’t energy work in the traditional sense.
It’s a conversation — with the body.
And bodies respond.

### In This Class You Will:

✨ Learn a specific Access Body Process you can use for life
✨ Both gift and receive the process (yes, you get sessions too!)
✨ Explore how judgment impacts the body
✨ Discover new tools for ease, vitality, and awareness
✨ Leave certified to practice this body process on others

No prior experience is required. Just a body. And a willingness.

### What Becomes Possible?

Many people report:
• Increased ease in chronic patterns
• Greater relaxation and presence
• Changes in long-held physical limitations
• A deeper sense of trust with their body

But more than anything — possibility.
What if your body has capacities you’ve never been shown how to access?

Spots are limited only by space - the sooner you sign up the sooner we can look for larger locations if required.

If you’ve been asking for more ease, more connection, more *aliveness* — this may be the invitation your body has been waiting for.

Would your body enjoy this?

A body process class is a way to experience a new energy. Each is uniquely different and contributes to the being. There are NO contraindications - if it pulls you in it's right for you that day.

This class will include the body process **Circuitry**!

Registration: https://www.consciousbeing.institute/event-details/body-process-class-circuitry

title: Walk—National Spongecake Day—Maggie Valley Starting at McCracken Corner Park
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
It's National Spongecake Day on August 23! If you will walk with me that day, I will bring some spongecake snacks to share at the end!

Meet at McCracken Corner Park, 56 State Rd 1307, Waynesville 28785 (Moody Farm Road/State Road 1307 intersects Soco Road twice; this is the eastern intersection with a traffic light further from Maggie Valley). We will meet at 2:00 p.m.

**Note: There is no restroom at the start point. Our route will pass a convenience store, and there is a restroom about halfway through the walk at Parham Memorial Park. Please plan accordingly.**

Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. The walk is pretty flat, all on pavement except for a short portion near the end. Tennis shoes are fine; walking poles aren't needed (although I plan to bring one). Bring *plenty of water* and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Strollers are fine.

We will walk up Soco Road to Parham Memorial Park (the western intersection of Moody Farm Road/State Road 1307 and Soco Road). Then we will walk along Moody Farm Road, with one short side excursion, back to the start point.

Hope to see you there!

title: Game Night @ Archetype West Asheville
description:
Asheville 20s-40s Social Group
\*\*This is a collaboration with the Asheville's Bored Game Geeks\*\*

Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!
**Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!**

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers!
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**.

**Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death!
No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.***

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary.

See you at the table!

title: Manifesting Self
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**Location Change:**
**Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**

Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??

Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.

Manifesting Self may sound a little out there. Trust me. It’s not. Whether we’ve been in the remote space for years, since the pandemic, or just recently, I’m certain it has changed each of us in ways we never thought possible. Let’s explore that together. The highs, the lows, and everywhere in between. And from there experience growth.

We are so excited to see you, again or for the first time!

title: Walk 3 Short, Easy Trails at Panther Creek State Park TN
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Panther Creek State Park is in Tennessee, just outside of Morristown. **We will meet at the entrance to the park.** The park covers approximately 1435 acres and is located on the shores of Cherokee Lake. The park offers a variety of recreational opportunities including camping, fishing, boating, picnicking, swimming, hiking, biking, and horseback riding.

The park boasts over 30 miles of world-class trails ranging from easy to difficult. Visitors are encouraged to Leave No Trace when using the trails. Hikers can enjoy a magnificent view of Cherokee Lake and the Cumberland Mountains.

We will do 2 hiking only trails and 1 hiking and biking trail. We will have to travel from trailhead to trailhead. I've tried to factor that into our time.

The Road to Recycling Trail is a 1.2 mile, easy, hiking only trail. This self-guided trail educates park visitors on the benefits of conserving natural resources. As such, there are signs along the trail. This trail was awarded the Governor's Greenways and Trails Stewardship Award in 2004.

The Seven Sinkholes Trail is a 0.6 mile loop, easy, hiking only trail. Sinkholes develop when rainfall dissolves the under-layer of porous limestone rock forming cavities. These cavities and depressions within the limestone gradually enlarge creating sinkholes. The trail meanders around seven distinct sinkholes before dipping into a lush valley of cedar and pine.

Old Wagon Trail is a 1 mile, easy, hiking and mountain biking trail. It appears on the map to be out-and-back 1 mile each way. It is the most popular trail at the park and is excellent for all ages and abilities. This trail follows the contour of Panther Creek and features a flat, wide surface. This is an excellent trail for the wildlife enthusiast, as many different birds and animals are frequently observed along the trail, especially in the early morning.

The park has restrooms in certain areas which we can visit before, between, and after the 3 walks. Dress appropriately for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. I believe tennis shoes are fine, unless it has rained recently, in which case you will probably want light hiking boots. Most won't want walking sticks, though I plan to take just one. As always, bring plenty of water and a protein snack. I have no information on limitations on dogs (although a park that has horses could hardly complain about dog owners who cleans up their pets' messes). Being easy trails, I would think trail strollers would work. Wheelchairs would probably work on Old Wagon Trail, although I'm not 100% certain.

I have no information on an entrance fee to the park. Come prepared just in case. The walk itself is free.

As you may surmise, I have not done this event previously. You are invited to come and try out this new place with me.

title: On National Read a Book Day, Let's Walk at Lake Junaluska
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
September 6 is National Read a Book Day. Right before we step-off, let's share with each other the title of a book we recommend the others read too. If you are able to "show and tell" bring the book with you, so much the better. Don't worry, we'll give you time to put the book back in your car before we step-off on the walk. (I don't want to carry a book on a 7 KM walk with hills!)

Gather at 2:00 at Lake Junaluska inside the Bethea Welcome Center. This will be a 7 KM/4 mile route. The walk does not just go around the lake, but up to Lambuth Inn, along the Rose Walk, and through the Nature Garden. The view from Inspiration Point is a must-see!

Dress for the weather. Consider a hat and sunscreen. Some people may want walking poles, especially for the walk up to Lambuth Inn; tennis shoes should be fine. It is particularly important that walkers bring a protein snack and **plenty of** **water**. Restrooms are available at the Welcome Center, at Lambuth Inn, and along the route. Dogs on leash are welcome. Strollers are ok.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.
